name: Partridge Soft Hackle
imitates: A small traditional soft hackle that suggests an emerging caddis or mayfly; the thread-twist hackle method lets you tie it very small.

steps.text: Start the thread and lay a piece of flat mylar tinsel under the hook, gold side up; fold it over the thread so it wraps silver side up.
Wrap the tinsel back to between the hook point and the barb, then forward over itself, and tie it off a third of a shank behind the eye.
Split a length of silk floss to one third of its thickness, tie it in and wrap a smooth two-layer abdomen back and forward.
Dub a small, tight ball-shaped thorax at the front of the abdomen, leaving room behind the eye.
Pick a partridge feather with a straight, square tip and stroke back the short fibers so the tips are even.
Cut the center stem a third of the way down to leave a V-shaped feather, and lay it on top of the shank with the tips about to the hook point.
Pinch the feather along the shank, take two soft turns of thread over it, then draw the thread tight so the torque spins the fibers evenly around the hook.
Trim the butt ends as close to the shank as possible.
Cover the stubs with neat thread wraps, whip finish and clip the thread. The finished fly shows a sparse, evenly spread hackle.
